question: The tissue-level reduction says the interior's mean conductance is an integral controller: d<G>/dt = -500*(<field> - fieldTransductionBias), with <field> rising as the tissue polarises. If that is the mechanism and not a coincidence of timescales, then fieldTransductionBias IS the set point, and moving it should move the whole trajectory in a predicted way.
registeredBefore: any set-point sweep existed; the runner is written after this file is committed
model: 1888, 11x11, hold 301, trained orders 0-3 code in every run; only fieldTransductionBias differs
sweep: bias = {0.6, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0, 1.1, 1.2, 1.4} x 5.0e-4, seven runs in one batch, 3000 iterations

definitions.firstPeak: maximum of the interior mean G over iterations 0-301, and the iteration it occurs
definitions.trough: minimum of the interior mean G over iterations 302-1300
definitions.secondPeak: maximum of the interior mean G from the trough to the end, and the iteration it occurs
definitions.selectivity: mean G over the 14 feature cells minus mean G over the 67 background cells, at that run's own second peak
definitions.meanField: the interior mean of the field each cell reads, eV averaged over its screened grid points
definitions.darkCount: interior cells with Vmem below -34.6 mV

P1.claim: the set point sets how far the tissue polarises before it turns
P1.criterion: the first peak of the interior mean G rises monotonically with bias, Spearman rho >= +0.9 at p < 0.05

P2.claim: and how long it takes to get there
P2.criterion: the iteration of the first peak rises monotonically with bias, Spearman rho >= +0.9 at p < 0.05

P3.claim: the turning point IS the set-point crossing, in every run
P3.criterion: for all seven runs, |first-peak iteration - first iteration at which meanField crosses that run's own bias| <= 2

P4.claim: the code has leverage only while the tissue sits near its set point, so leverage follows dwell time
P4.criterion: across the seven runs, phase3Duration correlates with selectivity at the second peak, Spearman rho >= +0.6

P5.claim: whether the tissue darkens at all is set by how far the controller lets it polarise
P5.criterion: the maximum interior darkCount over the run rises monotonically with bias, Spearman rho >= +0.9, and is strictly smaller at the lowest bias than at the trained bias

P6.claim: control -- the sweep changes nothing else
P6.criterion: the run at the trained bias reproduces the recorded trajectory exactly: first peak 1.421, trough at 585, second peak at 1765

notes: P3 is the load-bearing one: it asks whether the turning point is the set-point crossing by construction in every run, not just in the trained one. P1, P2 and P5 could all be produced by any monotone reparameterisation of the drive; P3 and P4 are what distinguish a closed loop with a set point from a drive that merely happens to rise and fall. A failure of P3 would say the aggregate ODE is an identity without mechanistic content.
